steps.text: Beat egg whites and salt in a large bowl until stiff peaks form. Lift beater straight up: egg whites should form stiff peaks that hold their shape.
Beat egg yolks in a separate large bowl.
Beat confectioners' sugar and butter together in a third large bowl until light and fluffy; beat in egg yolks and vanilla. Stir in nutmeg, cloves, allspice, and egg whites until well blended.
Scoop batter onto drink of choice.

raw_recipe.headline: Tom and Jerry Batter
raw_recipe.description: This Tom and Jerry batter recipe is a sweet, frothy vintage topping made with beaten raw eggs, sugar, vanilla, and warm spices for a festive favorite.

review.reviewBody:
This is also a family recipe of mine.
We put 2 TBLS with a 1/2 shot of run and a 1/2 shot of whiskey and add hot water. Stir - it's the best to warm you from the inside out. You can also make for kids without the alcohol.

This recipe is awesome and delicious. It does make a gargantuan amount. I made a quarter batch plenty for a small gathering. As such, I use this: 3 large eggs, separated, divided Pinch of salt 1 stick (1/4 lb) butter, room temperature 12 onces confectioners' sugar 1/4 teaspoon vanilla extract 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg 1/4 teaspoon ground cloves 1/4 teaspoon ground allspice I like to cream the butter and confectioners sugar, then incorporate the egg yolks one by one. I finished by folding the meringue into this mixture.

I quartered this recipe and added less butter and sugar and it is still great. Try it with 1.5 oz dark rum and .75 oz Tuaca or Velvet Falernum for even more spicy goodness. 

Here's what I did: 
3 eggs, 1/4 tsp of the spices, 8 oz confectioners sugar and only 4 oz butter. 
This still makes plenty for a party.

Been making this for years! On the 72 serving version (which actually will be roughly 36 as you’ll want to use at least 2 tbsp batter per large cup), I alter the recipe to 2 tsp nutmeg, 2 tsp allspice, 1 1/2 tsp clove and, most importantly, at least 1 tablespoon (NOT teaspoon) of a really good Madagascar Bourbon Vanilla. THEN it’s absolutely perfect!!!!!!

Delicious batter! Made half a batch and it scales down nicely. A half-batch makes about a quart. Freeze one pint, and use the other. I also added ground cardamom - 1/2 t for the posted recipe, or 1/4 t for the half-recipe. One shot brandy in a mug, followed by hot water then a heaping Tablespoon of batter. Stir, enjoy.

so I made this recipe but I only did a half batch cuz 3 lbs of sugar and a dozen eggs seemed like a lot to me.. but anyhow.. I made the half batch and I omitted the allspice and I added a dash of cinnamon, 2 tbsp. of honey and the seeds of 1 vanilla bean. I also replaces 1/2 a lb of powdered sugar for light brown sugar which gives it nice almost caramel tones.. we make ours with 1 shot of brandy and 1 shot of dark rum and boiling water.. tastes like xmas in a glass :)

My husband is from Wisconsin and described this drink really nostalgically and fondly since we don't live there anymore. The reason I'm giving this recipe 4 stars instead of 5 is because even though Tom and Jerries are supposed to be sweet, the recipe as is would be cloyingly over sweet. Based on other reviews and the New York Times recipe for Tom and Jerry batter I used 2/3 the amount of sugar called for, which turned out to be the perfect amount. When my husband finally got to taste, he said it was on the mark and that it tasted exactly like what he had growing up in his childhood.

Loved this recipe. Wonderful flavors. I have not had Tom and Jerry since leaving Iowa in mid 90s where I purchased batter from a grocery store. This tastes soooo much better. I made a half batch and did make 2 changes: I added cream of tartar to stabilize the egg whites; and I used a full tablespoon of vanilla. Thanks so much for sharing this recipe and thanks to all for your comments... such an enjoyable read. Merry Christmas and Happy New Year to all!

Perfect! Exactly as Mama Karla (Mamo) used to make it. One IMPORTANT note, though... Don't do the egg white step first as the instructions say. Separate the eggs and chill the whites white you mix the yolk "section." Keeping the whites "section" cold will keep it from getting "soupy." Otherwise, SPOT ON! 
P.S. Keeping it frozen and scooping it with an ice cream scoop will also eliminate the "soupy ness." cheers!!

Great recipe and a seasonal favorite at our house! We use white rum, brandy, and a splash of creme de cacao or coffee liqueur. For a kid friendly non-alcoholic version, use chocolate, caramel, or mocha coffee flavoring instead of liquor.

I’ve made several recipes over the years and this is by far the best! I will look no further! This is now kept, saved and will be enjoyed for years! Thank you allrecipes!❤️. We put one shot of brandy and one shot of rum into a mug, add about 3/4 cup of simmered hot water and top with about 3 T of batter. Stir lightly and sprinkle with cinnamon!

Same as our Wisconsin family recipe. We also use two heaping TBSP batter in a mug of hot water mit Schloss or with a shot... Traditionally we used brandy. But rum, bourbon, whiskey, all are great! We freeze the batter. And I also put it in freezer quart sized bags and freeze and give as gifts with a small shot bottle or two and sometimes a mug, too.

I haven't had this since I was a teen/young adult when I left Wisconsin. I added a little rum to the batter to help with the short term storage as it's a big batch. Made some with dark rum and some with brandy. Took me strait back home and warmed the old heart. It's was my native Texans wifes first time even hearing about these but she really liked them with tje brandy and hot milk. 10 out of 10.
Use Milk, not water. You will never go back. Guaranteed.

This is delish! So much better than the store-bought stuff. I did what another did and added cream of tartar as well as more vanilla. Mixed a heaping teaspoon with some dark rum and topped it off with boiling hot water. Soooo good!
This is the exact same recipe my mother made when I was a little girl back in the 50's. I have been making it for my family every Christmas since . It is wonderful just the way it is.
Just as I remembered from years ago up in Northwest Wisconsin. I like to mix mine with ginger Brandy it's quite delightful!
Fantastic batter mix with great spices. Less sweet than other mixes.
